chunks.content: ## Creating a Twist Panel in CLO: Step-by-Step Process This section explains how to create a twist panel in CLO using tools such as the plus point line tool, internal line tool, internal circle, twist tool, and simulation settings. Key terms include seam allowance, internal lines, twist extension, and fabric physical properties. ### Scoring and Defining Seam Allowance Reference Lines - Use the **Plus Point Line Tool** to score the panel; this marks the reference for the seam allowance position. - Switch to the **Edit Panel Tool**, then select the **Internal Line Tool**. - Add an internal line at the required position with a length between 1 to 8 mm. - To avoid extension, create an internal line parallel to the original. - This internal line serves as the reference for adding the seam allowance. ### Adding and Adjusting Internal Circles for Twist Positioning - Add an **Internal Circle** at the endpoint of the internal line. - Set the circle diameter to **10 mm** and confirm. - This circle marks the twist panel position to be fixed. - Copy and paste the circle to all necessary positions. - Separate points on the internal circle for easier handling. - Delete the unwanted half so only a **semi-circular fixed panel line** remains. ### Using the Twist Tool and Setting Extensions - Use the **Twist Tool** to add an extension at the center point of the semi-circular internal circle. - Switch to the **Select Move Twist Tool**. - Copy the first twist, then right-click to paste it at the corresponding positions below. - Multiple extension twists can be added this way. - Set the twist layer by hardening the middle panels and bringing them closer together. - Flatten the two-layer panels as needed. - Turn off simulation during this setup. ### Layer and Seam Settings for Twist Panels - Set the number of layers involved in sewing (typically two). - Use the **Add Point Division Tool** to add points on the edges to facilitate precise location. - Apply **Length Division** on the bottom edge to create a segment of **8 mm**, centered and aligned with the half-circle position. - Ensure seams on both ends of the panel line are fixed to the opposite side with careful attention to seam direction. - The middle section can have a slight separation for flexibility. ### 3D Adjustment and Particle Diameter Modification - Select the panel line and open the **3D Window**. - Move the panel line to the seam position; rotate the view and pull it out slightly. - Modify the **particle diameter** of the panel to adjust its visual and physical behavior. - Freeze the back panel to stabilize the simulation. - After adjustments, run the simulation and refine positioning as necessary. ### Applying Fabric Properties and Simulation - Apply the fabric intended for the panel line. - Duplicate the fabric and assign a **harder physical attribute** to observe the panel line effect in simulation. - Copy and repeat the process for remaining panel lines.

The process ensures precise positioning and realistic fabric behavior for garment detailing involving button loops or similar twisted panel features.
